target_customer: Consumers who use AI agents (shopping, food orders, reservations, tickets) and want to approve spending without sharing a real card number
problem: AI agents ask users to paste a real card number to complete purchases, which exposes the card and gives the agent unbounded spending power.
business_model: Consumer app issuing scoped one-time virtual cards; pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: Fintech, spend controls and virtual cards for AI agents

founders.name: Dasmer Singh
prior_employers: Cash App (Head of Product, Cash App Families)
founders.background_notes: Launch YC post says the idea came when an AI agent asked him to paste his credit card number to hold a reservation. Solo founder per YC page.

competitors.name: Crossmint agentic payments
competitors.what: Virtual Visa and Mastercard cards issued to AI agents

competitors.name: Agentcard (YC)
competitors.what: API for developers to issue single-use virtual Visa cards with fixed limits for agents

competitors.name: Oobit Agent Cards
competitors.what: Programmable cards for AI agents, USDT funded, aimed at businesses

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs card issuing through a partner, an iPhone approval flow and an MCP server; standard fintech engineering, with compliance and issuer relationships the hard parts for one founder.

defensibility.rationale: Several issuers and startups launched agent cards in the same months, and virtual card issuing is available through standard APIs, so copying is fast.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Within months of the batch, Ramp, Mercury (Aug 2026) and Corpay (Jul 2026) shipped agent card products per press, though aimed at businesses rather than consumers.

market_need_then: Agent shopping and booking tools were spreading in 2026 and users were being asked for raw card numbers; card networks and fintechs were launching agent payment products, showing demand and attention.

branding.domain_note: Uses useallowance.com rather than allowance.com; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: plain consumer voice in the Launch YC post

brand_strength.rationale: A search for the name returns mostly generic pocket money results, and no press about the brand was found; the site also promotes a related product called Alfie.

outcome_analysis: Allowance is a Spring 2026 company with a solo founder from Cash App Families, so founder market fit in consumer payments is clear. No outcome has occurred; no shutdown, acquisition or layoff reports were found. The main risk is that well funded issuers and card networks entered agent payments in the same months, which can compress a thin wedge.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (Neuronfeed, Fundup, PitchBook, FundedIQ, VCBacked) show a $500K round but disagree on stage (seed vs pre-seed) and date (April or June 2026); no company announcement found, so no round recorded. useallowance.com currently shows a product called Alfie by Allowance. Completeness pass: one 500K USD pre-seed recorded from FundedIQ (June 2026). It rests on a single database; Neuronfeed dates it January 2026 as seed, FundUp April 2026, and PitchBook names Neer Venture Partners and Y Combinator as investors.
